champion: Infiltrative ductal carcinoma of the breast
ordered_diagnoses: Infiltrative ductal carcinoma of the breast

facts.raw_span: A 48-year-old woman
type 2 diabetes
hypertension
bilateral breast lumps of one-week duration
no family history of breast or ovarian cancer
a 4 × 4 cm hard lump in the lower inner quadrant fixed to the chest wall
MRI showed a 3.8 × 3.5 cm irregular spiculated mass in the left breast suspicious for malignancy
a 2.3 × 1.5 cm well-defined lesion in the right breast with a type 1 contrast enhancement pattern (< 6% probability of malignancy)
bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy
poorly cohesive clusters of ductal cells with pleomorphism, hyperchromasia, and prominent nucleoli
infiltrative duct cell carcinoma that was estrogen- and progesterone-receptor positive
FNAC of the left axillary lymph node showed similar malignant cells

concepts.preferred_label: Infiltrative ductal carcinoma of the breast
concepts.why: The patient's left breast lump was found to be a 4 × 4 cm hard lump fixed to the chest wall, with MRI showing a 3.8 × 3.5 cm irregular spiculated mass suspicious for malignancy, and FNAC and core-needle biopsy confirming infiltrative ductal carcinoma.

The patient's right breast lump was found to be a firm, mobile 1 × 1 cm lump, with MRI showing a 2.3 × 1.5 cm well-defined lesion with a type 1 contrast enhancement pattern, and was suspected to be a fibroadenoma based on physical examination results.
The patient presented with bilateral breast lumps, with MRI showing suspicious masses in both breasts, and FNAC and core-needle biopsy confirming ductal carcinoma in both breasts.

rationales.F06: The presence of a hard lump fixed to the chest wall is highly suggestive of malignancy, specifically infiltrative ductal carcinoma.
rationales.F07: The MRI findings of an irregular spiculated mass are highly suspicious for malignancy, supporting the diagnosis of infiltrative ductal carcinoma.
rationales.F10: The cytological findings of poorly cohesive clusters of ductal cells with pleomorphism and hyperchromasia are characteristic of infiltrative ductal carcinoma.
rationales.F11: The diagnosis of infiltrative duct cell carcinoma that is estrogen- and progesterone-receptor positive is highly specific and supports the diagnosis of C01.
rationales.F12: The presence of similar malignant cells in the left axillary lymph node supports the diagnosis of infiltrative ductal carcinoma and suggests lymph node metastasis.

frontier_selector.champion: Infiltrative ductal carcinoma of the breast
frontier_selector.rationale: The left breast lump's characteristics, such as being fixed to the chest wall and having a spiculated mass on MRI, along with cytology and biopsy results confirming infiltrative duct cell carcinoma, strongly support this diagnosis. The presence of bilateral breast lumps and lymphadenopathy suggests the possibility of synchronous bilateral breast cancer, but the right breast lump's characteristics are more indicative of a benign lesion like fibroadenoma.
